objects.description: Data holder describing a single registered command-line flag, including its name, type, help text, current and default values, source filename, validator presence, default-state flag, and pointer to the live storage. Used by query/reporting APIs like GetAllFlags and DescribeOneFlag.

RAII helper that snapshots all flags on construction and restores any changed flags on destruction. Thread-safe to use, but direct concurrent access to flags whose values are restored by the destructor is unsafe. Uses a PIMPL (FlagSaverImpl) hidden in the library.

Helper used by DEFINE_* macros to register a flag at static initialization time. Provides a templated constructor specialized for supported flag types (bool, int32, uint32, int64, uint64, double, std::string). No other public API.
Enumeration controlling how SetCommandLineOptionWithMode applies a new value: set current value, set only if still default, or update default (and possibly current).

Tiny tag struct used solely for a compile-time assertion in DEFINE_bool to ensure bool and double have different sizes and to validate that the provided default value is actually a bool. Not used at runtime.

Helper used by DEFINE_string macro to ensure placement-new constructed string flag storages are properly destroyed at program teardown within the same translation unit. Holds raw pointers to the two storage buffers (current and default) and explicitly calls clstring destructors.
Fixed-width integer typedefs exported by gflags into its namespace for portability: int32, uint32, int64, uint64. These are aliases of standard C99 types (or platform-specific equivalents).
Unsigned 32-bit integer typedef within the gflags namespace. See int32 entry for details.
Signed 64-bit integer typedef within the gflags namespace. See int32 entry for details.
Unsigned 64-bit integer typedef within the gflags namespace. See int32 entry for details.
Typedef alias to std::string used internally by DEFINE_string/DECLARE_string machinery to decouple the macro expansion from any later redefinition of std::string.

functions.name: GFLAGS_NAMESPACE::RegisterFlagValidator
functions.signature: bool GFLAGS_NAMESPACE::RegisterFlagValidator(const bool* flag, bool (*validate_fn)(const char*, bool))
functions.description: Registers a validator callback for a boolean flag. The validator is invoked when the flag is set via command-line parsing or SetCommandLineOption, not when assigned directly. Returns true if registration succeeds, false if the pointer does not reference a command-line flag or a validator is already registered for that flag.
requirements: flag must point to a gflags-managed boolean flag variable (e.g., &FLAGS_name)
validate_fn must be a non-null function pointer taking (const char*, bool) and returning bool
If the validator returns false for the default value, ParseCommandLineFlags() will terminate the program
This function is safe to call at global construction time

functions.name: GFLAGS_NAMESPACE::GetAllFlags
functions.description: Populates OUTPUT with metadata for all registered command-line flags, sorted by defining file. Intended for introspection and reporting.
requirements: OUTPUT must be a non-null pointer to a vector to receive results
Do not call from within a flag validator (risk of deadlock, per header note)
This routine is relatively slow; use judiciously

functions.name: GFLAGS_NAMESPACE::ShowUsageWithFlags
functions.description: Prints usage information and all flags (like the --help behavior) to stdout, using argv0 for the program name.
requirements: argv0 should be the program name string (may be null-terminated C string)
Thread-safety not explicitly stated; typically used during initialization

functions.name: GFLAGS_NAMESPACE::ShowUsageWithFlagsRestrict
functions.signature: void GFLAGS_NAMESPACE::ShowUsageWithFlagsRestrict(const char* argv0, const char* restrict)
functions.description: Prints usage and flags to stdout, restricted to flags whose defining filename contains the given restrict substring.
requirements: argv0 should be the program name string
restrict may be null or a substring used to filter by filename

functions.name: GFLAGS_NAMESPACE::DescribeOneFlag
functions.description: Returns a pretty-printed, descriptive single-line (with line-breaks as needed) string for the specified flag, including its name, default/current values, and help text.
requirements: flag must be a valid CommandLineFlagInfo previously obtained (e.g., via GetAllFlags or GetCommandLineFlagInfo)

functions.name: GFLAGS_NAMESPACE::SetArgv
functions.signature: void GFLAGS_NAMESPACE::SetArgv(int argc, const char** argv)
functions.description: Stores a copy of argv and argv[0] for later retrieval via GetArgv*, ProgramInvocation* and related functions.
requirements: Must be called before any threads are spawned (thread-hostile)
argc must be non-negative; argv must point to an array of argc C strings (may be null-terminated strings)

functions.name: GFLAGS_NAMESPACE::GetArgvs
functions.description: Returns a const reference to the stored copy of argv as a vector of strings.

functions.name: GFLAGS_NAMESPACE::GetArgv

functions.name: GFLAGS_NAMESPACE::GetArgv0

requirements: Thread-safe only if SetArgv() was called before threads start

functions.name: GFLAGS_NAMESPACE::GetArgvSum

functions.name: GFLAGS_NAMESPACE::ProgramInvocationName

functions.name: GFLAGS_NAMESPACE::ProgramInvocationShortName

functions.name: GFLAGS_NAMESPACE::VersionString

functions.name: GFLAGS_NAMESPACE::GetCommandLineOption

functions.name: GFLAGS_NAMESPACE::GetCommandLineFlagInfo

functions.description: Sets the named flag’s value as if provided on the command line (mode SET_FLAGS_VALUE). Returns a non-empty string describing the new value on success, or an empty string on failure (e.g., unknown flag or invalid value).

value must be a non-null C string representing a valid value for that flag’s type

functions.name: GFLAGS_NAMESPACE::SetCommandLineOptionWithMode
functions.signature: std::string GFLAGS_NAMESPACE::SetCommandLineOptionWithMode(const char* name, const char* value, GFLAGS_NAMESPACE::FlagSettingMode set_mode)

functions.name: GFLAGS_NAMESPACE::CommandlineFlagsIntoString

prog_name should be the program name string used for diagnostics

functions.name: GFLAGS_NAMESPACE::SetUsageMessage
functions.description: Sets the program’s usage message (not including flags). Intended to be called during initialization before threads start.
requirements: Thread-hostile; must be called before any threads are spawned
usage should describe non-flag usage; flags are added automatically

functions.name: GFLAGS_NAMESPACE::SetVersionString

requirements: Thread-hostile; must be called before any threads are spawned

functions.signature: GFLAGS_NAMESPACE::uint32 GFLAGS_NAMESPACE::ParseCommandLineFlags(int* argc, char*** argv, bool remove_flags)
functions.description: Parses flags from argv, reordering argv to place flags first or removing them entirely if remove_flags is true. If a flag is defined multiple times, the last occurrence wins. Returns the index of the first non-flag argument.
requirements: argc must be a non-null pointer to the argument count
argv must be a non-null pointer to the argv array (pointer to array of C strings)
If remove_flags is true, flags are removed from argv
Should be called during program initialization before other threads start

functions.name: GFLAGS_NAMESPACE::ParseCommandLineNonHelpFlags
functions.signature: GFLAGS_NAMESPACE::uint32 GFLAGS_NAMESPACE::ParseCommandLineNonHelpFlags(int* argc, char*** argv, bool remove_flags)
functions.description: Parses all non-help/non-version flags from argv. Intended to be followed by HandleCommandLineHelpFlags(). Allows changing defaults between parsing and help emission. Returns index of first non-flag argument (1 if remove_flags is true).
requirements: argc and argv must be non-null pointers as in ParseCommandLineFlags
If remove_flags is true, function will return 1
Call HandleCommandLineHelpFlags() afterwards to process help/version flags

functions.name: GFLAGS_NAMESPACE::HandleCommandLineHelpFlags
functions.description: Processes help-related flags (and also handles --version, etc.). Typically invoked after ParseCommandLineNonHelpFlags to emit usage/help/version and exit if requested.
requirements: Should be called after ParseCommandLineNonHelpFlags during initialization
May terminate the process depending on flags present

functions.name: GFLAGS_NAMESPACE::AllowCommandLineReparsing
functions.description: Allows command line reparsing by disabling errors for unknown flags in the initial parse, so they may be recognized by a later parse (e.g., after loading modules that register additional flags).
requirements: Thread-hostile; must be called before any threads are spawned
Call before subsequent parses that should accept unknown flags for later handling

functions.name: GFLAGS_NAMESPACE::ReparseCommandLineNonHelpFlags
functions.description: Re-parses flags that were not yet recognized. Only flags registered since the last parse are recognized. Each flag value must be provided using '=' within the same argument (no separate following argument). Useful when dynamically loaded libraries register new flags.
requirements: Call after AllowCommandLineReparsing and an initial parse
Flag values must be provided with the '=' form (e.g., --flag=value)
Intended for handling flags from dynamically loaded libraries

functions.name: GFLAGS_NAMESPACE::ShutDownCommandLineFlags
functions.description: Cleans up memory allocated by flags to reduce noise in leak reports. Should be called only when the process is about to exit and no threads will access flags thereafter. Thread-hostile.
requirements: Only call when the process is about to exit
All threads that might access flags must be quiescent before calling
Do not reference flags after calling; behavior is undefined/unexpected
Not safe to run while multiple threads might be running

functions.name: google::HandleCommandLineCompletions
functions.description: Implements bash-style command line flag completion. Checks --tab_completion_word and, if set, generates and prints completion suggestions, then terminates the process (similar to --helpshort). Typically called early during startup after flag initialization, e.g., in HandleCommandLineHelpFlags().
requirements: Should be called after gflags has been initialized (flags registered and parsed state ready)
If --tab_completion_word is non-empty, this call will hijack the process to emit completions and then terminate

import random
import struct
import string
from typing import List

def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, choices: List[str]) -> str:
    return rng.choice(choices)

def _make_integer_string(rng: random.Random, bit_width: int) -> str:
    # Generate valid base-10 signed integer strings covering interesting ranges
    assert bit_width in (32, 64)
    if bit_width == 32:
        minv, maxv = -(2**31), 2**31 - 1
        interesting = [
            "0", "-0", "1", "-1", str(minv), str(maxv),
            str(2**15 - 1), str(-(2**15)), str(2**7 - 1), str(-(2**7)),
        ]
    else:
        minv, maxv = -(2**63), 2**63 - 1
        interesting = [
            "0", "-0", "1", "-1", str(minv), str(maxv),
            str(2**31 - 1), str(-(2**31)), str(2**15 - 1), str(-(2**15)),
        ]

    mode = rng.random()
    if mode < 0.5:
        # Pick from interesting constants
        s = rng.choice(interesting)
    elif mode < 0.8:
        # Uniform in a tight range around edges
        edge = rng.choice([minv, maxv, 0])
        delta = rng.randint(-1000, 1000)
        val = edge + delta
        if val < minv:
            val = minv
        if val > maxv:
            val = maxv
        s = str(val)
    else:
        # Full-range random within bounds
        val = rng.randint(minv, maxv)
        s = str(val)

    # Randomly add leading plus for non-negative (valid for many parsers but stays numeric)
    if s[0] not in ['-', '+'] and rng.random() < 0.2:
        s = "+" + s
    # Randomly add minimal leading zeros (still valid decimal) while keeping size modest
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        zeros = rng.randint(1, 3)
        core = s.lstrip('+')
        sign = '+' if s.startswith('+') else ''
        if core.startswith('-'):
            sign = '-'
            core = core[1:]
        s = sign + ("0" * zeros) + core
    return s

def _make_env_var_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Produce POSIX-like environment variable names: [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*
    first = rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + "_")
    length = rng.randint(1, 16)
    rest = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_") for _ in range(length))
    return first + rest

def _build_env_assignment(var: str, value: str) -> bytes:
    # Build lines like: VAR=123\n ready for parsers expecting flagfile-like or env-like content
    return f"{var}={value}\n".encode('ascii', errors='strict')

def _make_payload(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # This generator targets several stubs expecting integer strings and env var names.
    # We craft a small script-like buffer that contains multiple valid integer strings
    # and plausible environment variable assignments for 32-bit and 64-bit integers.

    parts: List[bytes] = []

    # Generate several integer strings alone, separated by newlines, to feed FUZZ_PARAM_STR
    count_integers = rng.randint(2, 6)
    for _ in range(count_integers):
        bw = 32 if rng.random() < 0.6 else 64
        parts.append((_make_integer_string(rng, bw) + "\n").encode('ascii'))

    # Add environment-like assignments for Int32FromEnv and Int64FromEnv usage
    count_env = rng.randint(2, 5)
    for _ in range(count_env):
        var = _make_env_var_name(rng)
        # Randomly decide 32 or 64 bit textual value (both valid integer strings)
        bw = 32 if rng.random() < 0.5 else 64
        val = _make_integer_string(rng, bw)
        parts.append(_build_env_assignment(var, val))

    # Also include some boolean-looking values for flags of type bool (as strings)
    bool_choices = ["true", "false", "1", "0", "t", "f", "T", "F"]
    count_bools = rng.randint(1, 3)
    for _ in range(count_bools):
        parts.append((rng.choice(bool_choices) + "\n").encode('ascii'))

    # Include a few floating-point strings for completeness (even if not required here)
    float_examples = [
        "0.0", "-0.0", "1.0", "-1.0", "3.1415926535", "1e10", "-2.5e-3",
        "1E300", "-1E300"
    ]
    count_floats = rng.randint(0, 2)
    for _ in range(count_floats):
        parts.append((rng.choice(float_examples) + "\n").encode('ascii'))

    blob = b''.join(parts)
    # Ensure size limit
    return blob[:4096]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    return _make_payload(rng)

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces a textual unsigned integer (base-10) as bytes.
# It targets stubs expecting environment variable values for Uint32FromEnv/Uint64FromEnv
# and value strings for SetCommandLineOption(_WithMode) when the flag type is uint32/uint64.
# Strategy: generate a variety of valid non-negative decimal integers, including:
# - Small numbers (0..9999)
# - Edge/near-edge values for uint32 and uint64
# - Random-length numeric strings with no leading '+' and only digits
# - Numbers with leading zeros (still valid decimal)
# All outputs are <= 4096 bytes.

UINT32_MAX = 2**32 - 1
UINT64_MAX = 2**64 - 1

# Precomputed interesting boundary and special values as strings
INTERESTING_NUMBERS: List[str] = [
    "0",
    "1",
    "2",
    "9",
    "10",
    "15",
    "16",
    "31",
    "32",
    "63",
    "64",
    "127",
    "128",
    "255",
    "256",
    "512",
    "1023",
    "1024",
    "4095",
    "4096",
    str(2**10 - 1),  # 1023
    str(2**10),      # 1024
    str(2**16 - 1),  # 65535
    str(2**16),      # 65536
    str(2**31 - 1),  # INT32_MAX
    str(2**31),
    str(UINT32_MAX - 1),
    str(UINT32_MAX),
    str(UINT32_MAX // 2),
    str(2**63 - 1),  # INT64_MAX
    str(2**63),
    str(UINT64_MAX - 1),
    str(UINT64_MAX),
    str(UINT64_MAX // 2),
]


def _rand_decimal_with_length(rng: random.Random, length: int) -> str:
    # Generate a decimal string of given length without leading '+'; allow leading zeros.
    if length <= 0:
        return "0"
    # First digit can be 0..9, but avoid empty/invalid.
    digits = [rng.choice(string.digits)]
    for _ in range(length - 1):
        digits.append(rng.choice(string.digits))
    # Avoid entirely empty or all non-digit; guaranteed digits only.
    s = ''.join(digits)
    # Avoid overly long leading zeros creating extreme length; strip only if entire string becomes empty
    # but keep at least one zero.
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        # Introduce some leading zeros intentionally
        zeros = '0' * rng.randint(1, 8)
        s = zeros + s
    # Normalize to avoid leading plus or whitespace (not generated anyway)
    return s


def _clamp_uint(s: str, bits: int) -> str:
    # Ensure s parses within the specified unsigned range; if too big, clamp to max.
    try:
        val = int(s, 10)
    except Exception:
        return "0"
    if val < 0:
        return "0"
    maxv = (1 << bits) - 1
    if val > maxv:
        val = maxv
    return str(val)


def _choose_interesting_number(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.5:
        # pick from interesting constants
        return rng.choice(INTERESTING_NUMBERS)
    elif choice < 0.8:
        # small range
        return str(rng.randint(0, 100000))
    else:
        # random length number possibly long; then clamp probabilistically to 32 or 64 bits
        length = rng.randint(1, 40)
        s = _rand_decimal_with_length(rng, length)
        # 50% keep as-is (valid arbitrary non-negative integer)
        # 25% clamp to uint32, 25% to uint64
        m = rng.random()
        if m < 0.25:
            return _clamp_uint(s, 32)
        elif m < 0.5:
            return _clamp_uint(s, 64)
        return s.lstrip('0') or '0'


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Decide a scenario to bias distribution toward exercising both uint32 and uint64 paths.
    scenario = rng.random()
    if scenario < 0.4:
        # Explicitly generate near uint32 bounds
        opts = [
            str(UINT32_MAX),
            str(max(UINT32_MAX - rng.randint(0, 1024), 0)),
            str(rng.randint(0, UINT32_MAX)),
            '0' * rng.randint(1, 5) + str(rng.randint(0, UINT32_MAX)),
        ]
        s = rng.choice(opts)
    elif scenario < 0.8:
        # Explicitly generate near uint64 bounds
        hi = UINT64_MAX
        # Use Python's big ints safely
        near = max(0, hi - rng.randint(0, 1 << 20))
        opts = [
            str(UINT64_MAX),
            str(near),
            str(rng.getrandbits(64)),
            '0' * rng.randint(1, 8) + str(rng.getrandbits(64)),
        ]
        s = rng.choice(opts)
    else:
        # Mixed/random interesting numbers
        s = _choose_interesting_number(rng)

    # Ensure it's a valid unsigned decimal string
    if not s or any(c not in string.digits for c in s):
        s = '0'

    # Trim to at most 4096 bytes (we keep it much smaller normally)
    if len(s) > 4096:
        s = s[:4096]
        # Avoid leading zeros turning into empty; ensure at least one digit remains
        s = s.lstrip('0') or '0'

    return s.encode('ascii')

import random
import math
from typing import List

# We generate textual representations of finite double values.
# Aim: cover diverse, valid forms that gflags/strtod will parse, including:
#  - plain integers and decimals
#  - leading/trailing zeros
#  - signs
#  - scientific notation with various exponent formats and signs
#  - special edge magnitudes within finite range (close to 0, subnormal-ish, large but < 1e308)
#  - fixed and scientific formatting variations
# The output is bytes for FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME inputs.
# Keep size <= 4096 bytes.

_MAX_LEN = 4096

_DEF_FORMS = [
    "int",           # e.g., "0", "42", "-7"
    "fixed",         # e.g., "3.14159", "-0.125"
    "sci",           # e.g., "1.23e10", "-4e-5"
    "leadzero",      # e.g., "000123.4500"
    "trailzero",     # e.g., "12.340000"
    "no_int_part",   # e.g., ".5", "-.0"
    "no_frac_part",  # e.g., "1.", "-2."
]

# Interesting finite magnitudes to exercise parsing and range handling
_INTERESTING_DOUBLES: List[float] = [
    0.0, -0.0,
    1.0, -1.0,
    1e-308, -1e-308,   # near min normal/subnormal boundary
    5e-324, -5e-324,   # tiny subnormals (may underflow to 0 in some prints)
    1e-300, -1e-300,
    1e300, -1e300,     # large but finite
    3.141592653589793,
    -2.718281828459045,
    6.02214076e23,
    -9.10938356e-31,
]

def _rand_sign(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return "-" if rng.random() < 0.5 else ""

def _fmt_int(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose from interesting ints and random range
    choices = [0, 1, -1, 2, -2, 10, -10, 123456789, -123456789]
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        n = rng.choice(choices)
    else:
        n = rng.randint(-10**9, 10**9)
    return str(n)

def _fmt_fixed(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Compose integer and fractional parts with variable precision
    sign = _rand_sign(rng)
    int_part = str(rng.randint(0, 10**6))
    # Ensure at least one digit in fractional part
    prec = rng.randint(1, 12)
    frac = ''.join(str(rng.randint(0, 9)) for _ in range(prec))
    return f"{sign}{int_part}.{frac}"

def _fmt_sci(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    sign = _rand_sign(rng)
    # mantissa with 1 to 3 digits before decimal, 0..10 after
    a = str(rng.randint(0, 9))
    b_len = rng.randint(0, 10)
    b = ''.join(str(rng.randint(0, 9)) for _ in range(b_len))
    mant = a if b_len == 0 else f"{a}.{b}"
    e_sign = '+' if rng.random() < 0.5 else '-'
    exp = rng.randint(0, 308)
    # Randomly choose e or E
    echar = 'e' if rng.random() < 0.5 else 'E'
    return f"{sign}{mant}{echar}{e_sign}{exp}"

def _fmt_leadzero(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    sign = _rand_sign(rng)
    zeros = '0' * rng.randint(1, 6)
    int_part = str(rng.randint(0, 9999))
    prec = rng.randint(0, 8)
    if prec == 0:
        return f"{sign}{zeros}{int_part}"
    frac = ''.join(str(rng.randint(0, 9)) for _ in range(prec))
    return f"{sign}{zeros}{int_part}.{frac}"

def _fmt_trailzero(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    sign = _rand_sign(rng)
    int_part = str(rng.randint(0, 9999))
    zeros = '0' * rng.randint(1, 8)
    return f"{sign}{int_part}.{zeros}"

def _fmt_no_int_part(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    sign = _rand_sign(rng)
    prec = rng.randint(1, 12)
    frac = ''.join(str(rng.randint(0, 9)) for _ in range(prec))
    return f"{sign}.{frac}"

def _fmt_no_frac_part(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    sign = _rand_sign(rng)
    int_part = str(rng.randint(0, 10**6))
    return f"{sign}{int_part}."

def _fmt_from_float(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose an interesting float and print in various ways
    x = rng.choice(_INTERESTING_DOUBLES)
    # Ensure finite and not NaN
    if not math.isfinite(x):
        x = 0.0
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.34:
        # Default repr-like with controlled magnitude to avoid inf/NaN
        return f"{x:.17g}"
    elif choice < 0.67:
        # Scientific with specified precision
        prec = rng.randint(1, 17)
        return f"{x:.{prec}e}"
    else:
        # Fixed with some precision (may be long, but bounded)
        prec = rng.randint(0, 10)
        return f"{x:.{prec}f}"

def _generate_float_string(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Bias toward diverse forms, mixing constructed and formatted-from-float
    forms = list(_DEF_FORMS) + ["from_float"] * 3
    form = rng.choice(forms)
    if form == "int":
        s = _fmt_int(rng)
    elif form == "fixed":
        s = _fmt_fixed(rng)
    elif form == "sci":
        s = _fmt_sci(rng)
    elif form == "leadzero":
        s = _fmt_leadzero(rng)
    elif form == "trailzero":
        s = _fmt_trailzero(rng)
    elif form == "no_int_part":
        s = _fmt_no_int_part(rng)
    elif form == "no_frac_part":
        s = _fmt_no_frac_part(rng)
    else:
        s = _fmt_from_float(rng)

    # Clamp extremely long strings just in case (but keep valid number)
    if len(s) > _MAX_LEN:
        s = s[:_MAX_LEN]
    return s

# Public API

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Optionally embed surrounding whitespace or plus sign variations that are valid for strtod
    s = _generate_float_string(rng)

    # Randomly add leading/trailing whitespace (valid for C strtod parsing)
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        lead_ws = rng.choice(["", " ", "\t", "\n", "\r\n"]) * rng.randint(0, 2)
        trail_ws = rng.choice(["", " ", "\t", "\n"]) * rng.randint(0, 2)
        s = f"{lead_ws}{s}{trail_ws}"

    # Randomly add explicit plus sign if not already signed
    if rng.random() < 0.3 and s and s.lstrip()[0] not in ['-', '+']:
        s = "+" + s

    # Ensure non-empty and within bounds
    if not s:
        s = "0.0"
    if len(s) > _MAX_LEN:
        s = s[:_MAX_LEN]

    return s.encode('ascii', errors='strict')

import random
from typing import List

def _pick_bool_string(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Valid boolean strings per API, case-sensitive.
    vals: List[str] = ["0", "1", "t", "T", "f", "F", "true", "false"]
    return rng.choice(vals)

def _make_env_var_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Portable env var: [A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*, 1..32 chars
    first_chars = "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz_"
    rest_chars = first_chars + "0123456789"
    length = rng.randint(1, 32)
    name = rng.choice(first_chars)
    name += "".join(rng.choice(rest_chars) for _ in range(length - 1))
    return name

def _maybe_embed_in_flag_assignment(rng: random.Random, val: str) -> bytes:
    # Sometimes embed the boolean string in common contexts used by the stubs:
    # - as a standalone value
    # - as part of --flag=value lines (for ReadFlagsFromString)
    # - multiple lines with comments and whitespace
    choice = rng.randint(0, 4)
    if choice == 0:
        return val.encode()
    elif choice == 1:
        # Single flag assignment
        flagname = _make_env_var_name(rng).lower()
        line = f"--{flagname}={val}\n"
        return line.encode()
    elif choice == 2:
        # Multiple assignments including duplicates; last one wins
        flagname = _make_env_var_name(rng).lower()
        lines = []
        n = rng.randint(2, 6)
        for i in range(n):
            vv = _pick_bool_string(rng) if i < n - 1 else val
            # Add optional spaces around '=' and before value
            pre = "" if rng.random() < 0.5 else " "
            post = "" if rng.random() < 0.5 else " "
            lines.append(f"--{flagname}{pre}={post}{vv}")
        return ("\n".join(lines) + "\n").encode()
    elif choice == 3:
        # Include comments and blank lines
        flagname = _make_env_var_name(rng).lower()
        lines = ["# autogenerated flagfile", "", f"--{flagname}={val}"]
        return ("\n".join(lines) + "\n").encode()
    else:
        # CSV-like list containing the boolean string (useful as generic string input)
        parts = ["alpha", val, "beta", _pick_bool_string(rng)]
        return (",".join(parts)).encode()

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Primary valid boolean string for this buffer
    val = _pick_bool_string(rng)

    # With some probability, construct an environment-style assignment payload
    # that the target can use for BoolFromEnv, else provide the raw value or
    # flagfile-like lines which are valid boolean representations in context.
    mode = rng.randint(0, 5)
    if mode == 0:
        # Raw boolean string
        payload = val.encode()
    elif mode == 1:
        # NAME=VALUE style common in env contexts (though the fuzzer supplies only bytes)
        name = _make_env_var_name(rng)
        payload = f"{name}={val}".encode()
    elif mode == 2:
        # Just the env var name; some paths may use the provided name separately
        payload = _make_env_var_name(rng).encode()
    else:
        # Flag assignment or composite contexts
        payload = _maybe_embed_in_flag_assignment(rng, val)

    # Ensure size limit
    if len(payload) > 4096:
        payload = payload[:4096]
    return payload

import random
import struct
import sys
from typing import List

# This generator targets gflags stubs that consume arbitrary byte strings for:
# - string flag values
# - usage/version strings
# - environment variable names and values (var names must be [A-Za-z0-9_]+)
# It returns a single bytes buffer that, when used by the fuzzer to source
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR/FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME, provides multiple interesting, valid strings.
#
# Strategy:
# - Produce a concatenation of several length-prefixed strings so the fuzzing
#   harness can slice from the buffer to obtain different strings.
# - Include diverse content: ASCII, UTF-8 multibyte, long/short lengths, edge
#   cases (empty, very long but <= 512/128 typical caps), numeric-only, paths,
#   shell-like values, booleans, numbers, floating points, JSON-like text, and
#   repeated characters.
# - Also provide valid environment variable names ([A-Za-z0-9_]+) by including
#   several candidates in the set.
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

def _lp(s: bytes) -> bytes:
    # 16-bit little-endian length prefix for easy slicing by the harness.
    # If string is too long for 16-bit, truncate to 65535.
    if len(s) > 0xFFFF:
        s = s[:0xFFFF]
    return struct.pack('<H', len(s)) + s

def _rand_ascii(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    n = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    alphabet = (
        'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz'
        'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ'
        '0123456789'
        ' _-./:@,'
    )
    return ''.join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n)).encode('utf-8')

def _rand_utf8(r: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Mix ASCII with multibyte UTF-8 sequences
    choices = [
        'αβγδεζηθικλμνξοπρστυφχψω',
        '汉字測試中文日本語かなカナ',
        '🙂🙃😉😊😇🥳🤖✨⚙️🔥',
        '€£¥₿₩₹₽',
    ]
    s = []
    target = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    while len(''.join(s)) < target:
        if r.random() < 0.6:
            s.append(_rand_ascii(r, 1, 6).decode('utf-8', 'ignore'))
        else:
            s.append(r.choice(choices))
    out = ''.join(s)[:target]
    return out.encode('utf-8', 'ignore')

def _env_var_name_candidates(r: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    names = [
        b'HOME', b'PATH', b'TEMP', b'USER', b'LANG', b'GFLAGS_TEST', b'A', b'Z9_', b'__X__',
    ]
    # Random valid names [A-Za-z0-9_]+
    for _ in range(6):
        n = r.randint(1, 24)
        alphabet = 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789_'
        names.append(''.join(r.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n)).encode('ascii'))
    return names

def _paths(r: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    # Potential filenames for FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME or general strings
    base = [b'/tmp/file.txt', b'/etc/hosts', b'./relative/path', b'../up/one', b'C:\\temp\\file.log']
    # Construct some random-ish paths
    for _ in range(5):
        parts = []
        depth = r.randint(1, 5)
        for __ in range(depth):
            parts.append(_rand_ascii(r, 1, 8).replace(b' ', b'_'))
        base.append(b'/' + b'/'.join(parts))
    return base

def _numbers(r: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    ints = [str(v).encode('ascii') for v in [0, 1, -1, 2147483647, -2147483648, 4294967295, 9223372036854775807, -9223372036854775808]]
    # Random ints
    for _ in range(6):
        ints.append(str(r.randint(-2**63, 2**63-1)).encode('ascii'))
    # Doubles
    doubles = [b'0.0', b'-0.0', b'1.0', b'-1.0', b'3.1415926535', b'2.99792458e8', b'-1e-9', b'1e300', b'-1e300']
    for _ in range(4):
        mant = r.uniform(-1e6, 1e6)
        exp = r.randint(-300, 300)
        doubles.append(('{:.12g}e{:+d}'.format(mant, exp)).encode('ascii'))
    return ints + doubles

def _bools() -> List[bytes]:
    return [b'true', b'false', b'T', b'F', b'1', b'0']

def _jsonlike(r: random.Random) -> bytes:
    kvs = []
    for _ in range(r.randint(2, 6)):
        k = _rand_ascii(r, 3, 10).decode('ascii').replace('"', '')
        if r.random() < 0.3:
            v = '"{}"'.format(_rand_ascii(r, 0, 8).decode('ascii').replace('"', ''))
        elif r.random() < 0.5:
            v = str(r.randint(-1000, 1000))
        else:
            v = random.choice(['true', 'false'])
        kvs.append('"{}":{}'.format(k, v))
    return ('{' + ','.join(kvs) + '}').encode('utf-8')

def _repeated(r: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    chs = [b'A', b'\n', b'\t', b' ', b'_', b'X']
    out = []
    for c in chs:
        out.append(c * r.randint(1, 64))
    return out

def _usage_samples(r: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    base = [
        b"Usage: prog [options] <input>\n",
        b"usage: tool --flag=value [--help] [--version]\n",
        b"Run with --helpshort to see common flags.\n",
    ]
    extra = _rand_ascii(r, 10, 120)
    base.append(extra)
    # Ensure <=512 typical cap used by stub
    base = [b[:512] for b in base]
    return base

def _version_samples(r: random.Random) -> List[bytes]:
    base = [b"1.0.0", b"v2.3.4", b"2026.01", b"beta-7", b"release-candidate"]
    base.append(_rand_ascii(r, 3, 40))
    return [b[:128] for b in base]

def _compose_buffer(chunks: List[bytes]) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    for s in chunks:
        lp = _lp(s)
        if len(out) + len(lp) > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        out += lp
    return bytes(out)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    chunks: List[bytes] = []

    # Edge cases first
    chunks.append(b'')  # empty string
    chunks.append(b'\x00')  # string containing NUL

    # Valid environment variable names and values
    for name in _env_var_name_candidates(r):
        chunks.append(name)
    # Some environment values
    chunks.extend([
        b'/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/local/bin',
        b'/tmp',
        b'en_US.UTF-8',
        _rand_utf8(r, 1, 40),
        _rand_ascii(r, 1, 80),
    ])

    # Paths
    chunks.extend(_paths(r))

    # Numbers for numeric flags
    chunks.extend(_numbers(r))

    # Boolean literals for bool flags
    chunks.extend(_bools())

    # Usage messages and versions
    chunks.extend(_usage_samples(r))
    chunks.extend(_version_samples(r))

    # JSON-like and shell-like content
    chunks.append(_jsonlike(r))
    chunks.append(b'KEY=VALUE')
    chunks.append(b'--flag=value')
    chunks.append(b'--another_flag=123')

    # UTF-8, repeated, long string (bounded)
    chunks.append(_rand_utf8(r, 20, 200))
    chunks.extend(_repeated(r))
    long_str = _rand_ascii(r, 300, 600)
    chunks.append(long_str)

    # A few random short strings
    for _ in range(10):
        if r.random() < 0.5:
            chunks.append(_rand_ascii(r, 0, 32))
        else:
            chunks.append(_rand_utf8(r, 0, 32))

    # Compose into length-prefixed blob so the harness can parse multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls
    buf = _compose_buffer(chunks)

    # Ensure non-empty output
    if not buf:
        buf = _lp(b'')

    return buf

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: environment variable name
# Constraints inferred from stubs and description:
# - Non-empty
# - Portable charset: [A-Za-z0-9_]
# - No '=' or NUL
# - Stubs sanitize to [A-Za-z0-9_] anyway; providing already-sanitized names avoids unintended collisions
# Coverage goals:
# - Vary name length (short, typical, long but <= 255 which is common limit per POSIX recommendation)
# - Mix starting with letter/underscore/digit (some libc allows leading digits; we still stick to portable set)
# - Include common prefixes that may interact with libraries: PATH, HOME, TMP, LANG, LC_ALL, USER, PWD, SHELL, TERM
# - Randomized suffixes to avoid overwriting same env across runs
# - Ensure size <= 4096 bytes

SAFE_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_"
COMMON_PREFIXES = [
    "PATH", "HOME", "TMP", "TMPDIR", "LANG", "LC_ALL", "USER", "USERNAME",
    "PWD", "SHELL", "TERM", "TZ", "HOSTNAME", "LOGNAME", "DISPLAY",
    "DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH", "LD_LIBRARY_PATH", "GFLAGS_TEST", "APP_CONFIG",
]

def _rand_env_name(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose a strategy to vary coverage
    strat = rng.randrange(6)
    if strat == 0:
        # Pure random of moderate length
        length = rng.randint(3, 24)
        return ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(length))
    elif strat == 1:
        # Long name near typical limits (<= 255)
        length = rng.randint(60, 180)
        return ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(length))
    elif strat == 2:
        # Very short name
        length = rng.randint(1, 2)
        return ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(length))
    elif strat == 3:
        # Common prefix with random suffix
        prefix = rng.choice(COMMON_PREFIXES)
        suffix_len = rng.randint(0, 20)
        suffix = ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(suffix_len))
        return prefix if not suffix else prefix + '_' + suffix
    elif strat == 4:
        # Starts with underscore, then random
        length = rng.randint(5, 32)
        return '_' + ''.join(rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(length - 1))
    else:
        # Numeric-heavy
        length = rng.randint(4, 30)
        s = [rng.choice(string.digits)]  # allow leading digit; still valid for getenv
        s += [rng.choice(SAFE_CHARS) for _ in range(length - 1)]
        return ''.join(s)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Produce a single environment variable name per invocation, as bytes without NUL.
    # Ensure non-empty and within size limit.
    name = _rand_env_name(rng)
    if not name:
        name = "X"

    # Truncate conservatively to avoid extreme sizes; keep <= 255 bytes.
    name = name[:255]

    # Encode to UTF-8 bytes (ASCII subset), ensure total <= 4096
    data = name.encode('ascii', errors='ignore')
    if not data:
        data = b"X"
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]

    return data
